adult-korean-adoptees-in-europe-document.core: Posted in last 7 days Adult Korean Adoptees in Europe - Document Falsification Experiences European KADS Please Share Your Stories: Korean Broadcasting System (KBS) will soon be travelling to Denmark to conduct interviews with adoptees and Danish authorities. KBS is South Korea’s national public-service broadcaster, equivalent to DR in Denmark, the BBC in the UK, and France Télévisions in France. As part of its ongoing work on adoption, KBS would like to hear from many more adult Korean adoptees. In collaboration with us, they have therefore developed a short questionnaire. Their focus is on document falsification: what documents have been falsified and how, the consequences this has had for adoptees, and what we would like to see happen in the future. The interviews conducted in Denmark, together with the findings from the questionnaire, will be featured in the evening news broadcasts as well as in online articles. Participation is anonymous. Only statistical data will be used to describe the circumstances of adoptees in general. Any quotations from adoptees will be published anonymously. Please note that the questionnaire will only be open until 11:59 PM KST on 4 December. We strongly encourage all adult Korean adoptees to participate. You can complete the questionnaire in either English or French: In English English version https://lnkd.in/ei77XEQq En français https://lnkd.in/eEguHhAg Chères toutes, chers tous, La Korean Broadcasting System (KBS) se rendra prochainement au Danemark afin de réaliser des entretiens avec des personnes adoptées ainsi qu'avec les autorités danoises. KBS est le radiodiffuseur public national de Corée du Sud, l'équivalent de DR au Danemark, de la BBC au Royaume-Uni et de France Télévisions en France. Dans le cadre de son travail continu sur l'adoption, KBS souhaite recueillir les témoignages d'un plus grand nombre d'adultes coréens adoptés. En collaboration avec nous, la chaîne a donc élaboré un court questionnaire. Le questionnaire porte principalement sur la falsification de documents : quels documents ont été falsifiés et de quelle manière, quelles conséquences cela a eues pour les personnes adoptées, et ce que nous souhaitons voir se réaliser à l'avenir. Les entretiens réalisés au Danemark, ainsi que les résultats du questionnaire, seront présentés dans les journaux télévisés du soir et dans des articles publiés en ligne. La participation est anonyme. Seules des données statistiques seront utilisées afin de décrire de manière générale la situation des personnes adoptées. Toute citation éventuelle de personnes adoptées sera publiée de manière anonyme. Veuillez noter que le questionnaire ne sera accessible que jusqu'au 4 décembre à 23 h 59 (heure de Corée, KST). Nous encourageons vivement toutes les personnes adultes adoptées d'origine coréenne à participer. neurodivergent-and-neurotypical-adults-e.headline: Neurodivergent & Neurotypical Adults - Emotional Experience - Podcast
neurodivergent-and-neurotypical-adults-e.author: Deborah McPhilemy
neurodivergent-and-neurotypical-adults-e.core: Posted in last 7 days Neurodivergent & Neurotypical Adults - Emotional Experience - Podcast Would you like to be a guest on my Feeling Differently podcast? For 23 years, I've been teaching emotional intelligence, believing that the way I experienced emotions was much the same as everyone else's. Then, at the age of 58, I discovered I had ADHD. And suddenly, I had more questions than answers. Do we all experience empathy in the same way? Can some people regulate their emotions more easily than others? When we tell someone to change their thinking to change their feelings, does that actually work for everyone? What happens inside us when we experience rejection, criticism, excitement, disappointment or even someone else's sadness? I want to find out! I'm looking for everyday people, both neurotypical and neurodivergent, who would be willing to join me on my Feeling Differently podcast for an open, relaxed and curious conversation about how they experience emotions and navigate everyday life. You don't need to be an expert, have an extraordinary story or know anything about emotional intelligence. I'm simply interested in your personal experience of being you. I'll be asking my guests the same core questions to explore where our experiences are similar, where they differ and what we might learn from one another. There are no right or wrong answers, and this isn't about assessing or judging anyone's emotional intelligence. It's about understanding each other better. Perhaps we've been assuming that we all feel the same things in the same way. And perhaps we don't. If you'd like to be part of this exploration, regardless of your age (18+), gender or neurotype, please send me a private message and I will send you a link to book a slot so we can chat I'd love to hear from you. ❤️

funeral-and-bereavement-professionals-ma.author: Alison (McClintock) Warner
funeral-and-bereavement-professionals-ma.core: Posted in last 7 days Funeral & Bereavement Professionals - Managing Death Admin I'm launching 'Sitting with it,’ a new series of short, honest conversations with professionals and practitioners in the grief and funeral space. They're part of my new Substack _before_&_after grief magazine. And their goal is simple. To answer the questions people don't want to face or ask, and provide more understanding of the resources and options that are out there. And we're kicking things off with a big one. Managing death admin. I'm really proud that my first interview is with Emma Knewstub, Director of Laurelo Probate, a family-run company that has won a gold award for compassionate care of customers from Hospice UK. 56% of adults in the UK don't have a will 53% are aged between 50-64 (until this year I was one of them) In 2025, 43,108 letters of administration were granted to families of loved ones who died intestate; and that figure has increased 50% in just two years. Emma has first-hand experience of what this means; her brother died suddenly without a will. She talks about the impact that had on her and her family; how it made her even more determined to make a difference in how probate is managed, and offers 3 tips on what to do if you want to get some plans in place. You can watch her interview below. And if you have a question you'd like answered, or would like to take part in the 'Sitting with it' series, you can get in touch with me via DM, I'd love to hear from you.

nz-public-sector-decisionmakers-mbie-bio.headline: NZ Public Sector Decision-Makers - MBIE Biometric Restart Sign-Off
nz-public-sector-decisionmakers-mbie-bio.author: Todd Scott
nz-public-sector-decisionmakers-mbie-bio.core: Posted in last 7 days NZ Public Sector Decision-Makers - MBIE Biometric Restart Sign-Off Nine planned go-live dates for one government IT project. The NZ Project Tracker is now public, and if, like me, you’ve ever wondered who has to answer for wasted public money, I’d start with what happened in the four weeks between two decisions. In October 2023, an independent review raised warnings about MBIE’s Biometric Capability Update. The project was paused. Four weeks later, it was back on. What changed in those four weeks? Which warnings had been addressed, and who had the authority to give the go-ahead? Kaleb Francis and the team have built a timeline that lets anyone click through all nine planned go-live dates and see the records behind them. They’ve named the officials involved and shown what each person actually did. Where official accounts disagree about who approved a decision, you can read both accounts and judge for yourself. Having your name in the minutes is a long way from signing off a restart. My view is that when a government department restarts a project after an independent review raises warnings, taxpayers should be able to see who signed off, which risks were still open and why proceeding was justified. Would you be satisfied with “MBIE approved the restart”, or would you expect a name and a written reason? I’d particularly like to hear from people who’ve had to make that call. What did you put on the record? https://lnkd.in/gDYA2seM
